sent_subject: Ember Yoga: homepage + booking teardown (prioritized fixes)
sent:
Priya —

We looked at emberyoga.example this morning. The biggest conversion tax is the “Book a class” click opening a new Mindbody tab and asking for an account before showing value.

Prioritized fixes:

P1. Make the intro offer the default path.
– Replace the hero CTA with “Start 30 days for £39” (primary), keep “See timetable” as secondary.
– Mirror “Start 30 days” in the top nav and in the footer.

P2. Keep the flow on-site until commitment.
– Embed your timetable/checkout or use a lightbox; avoid a new tab.
– Where possible, deep‑link with the Intro Offer pre‑selected so new clients don’t hit a price wall first.

P3. Add a “Beginner or Regular?” chooser under the hero.
– “I’m new” → three recommended classes this week, first‑visit tips, and the Intro Offer CTA.
– “I practise regularly” → timetable and 10‑class pack.

P4. Replace generic quotes with specific, local social proof next to CTAs.
– Short stories that name a studio/teacher and an outcome (e.g., “4 weeks on Beginner in Hackney, back pain gone”) outperform generic praise. Current best practice in UK studio sites backs this.

P5. Reduce first‑timer doubts in microcopy.
– Next to every primary CTA: “Mats/towels available • arrive 10 min early • heat and non‑hot options • showers/lockers.”

P6. Guide choice on the timetable.
– Default to “Today” and the nearest studio; add tags like “Good for beginners” and “Most booked this week.”

If helpful, we can share an annotated wireframe of the hero + chooser, sample testimonial prompts to collect the right stories, and two booking-flow options that reduce account friction while keeping Mindbody.

Count first‑class bookings from web as your north star; watch the drop from hero click → class selected → checkout started → paid. Fixes P1–P3 directly compress that gap.
